name: gnunet
desc: Framework for distributed, secure and privacy-preserving applications
why: A privacy-preserving peer-to-peer framework with its own protocols, a door into distributed networking most people never see.

brief.what_it_is: GNUnet is a network protocol stack and framework for building secure, distributed, and privacy-preserving applications. The homepage describes it as a replacement for the conventional Internet protocol stack, offering components for addressing, encrypted channels with routing and resource discovery, and naming. The executables list includes tools such as gnunet-gns, gnunet-vpn, gnunet-cadet, gnunet-fs, gnunet-messenger and gnunet-identity. I did not see the input or output formats of these tools in the pages I read.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage argues that metadata such as who talks to whom, when, how often and how much is exposed even under transport encryption, and that the Internet was not designed with security in mind. It also says every P2P project re-invents common components, which multiplies vulnerabilities.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage describes GNUnet as a self-organizing network that offers a metadata-preserving foundation with components for addressing, reliable encrypted channels, routing, resource discovery and naming. It says the network avoids a public ledger and uses decentralization only where it adds value. I did not find a detailed mechanism description in the pages I read.
brief.install_notes: I did not read the Installation section of the docs (docs.gnunet.org lists an Installation page, which I did not fetch). The brew metadata gave no caveats. The docs index shows versioned docs for branches v0.20.x through v0.27.x plus master, so pick the version that matches your needs.
brief.standout: Unlike most P2P projects, GNUnet is presented as a shared protocol stack and framework rather than a single app, with a stated goal of hiding metadata and avoiding blockchain-style consensus. Its roughly 50 executables expose many subsystems, and the homepage says the work rests on almost two decades of academic research.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as I can tell. The homepage's latest news lists GNUnet 0.29.0 dated 2026-08-20, GNUnet 0.28.0 dated 2026-07-17, and libgnunetchat 0.8.0 dated 2026-07-18. I did not see a last commit date. The GitHub mirror URL I tried returned 404.
brief.caveats: The homepage was reachable, but the GitHub repository URL I tried returned 404, so I have no README. The docs index had no commands and no install steps. The brew description is a single line and I saw no caveats there. I did not verify the license beyond the homepage's claim of free software.
quotes: GNUnet is a network protocol stack for building secure, distributed, and privacy-preserving applications.
Your metadata is just as revealing as the actual content; and it gets exposed on the Internet.
GNUnet does not require a decentralized, public ledger.
